value.rationale: Normalized finite-window generator design is the concrete worst-case stability problem for continuous dynamical frames. The theorem solves the entire one-vector all-horizon optimization for every real simple-spectrum contraction semigroup dimension, including strict uniqueness, explicit time-dependent spectral weights, and exact sharp lower bound, a stronger structural classification than finite experiments or a single special case. At rates (1,2), the optimal weights change from (1/2,1/2) for T↓0 to (7/17,10/17) for T→∞; thus the arbitrary finite-time formula captures genuinely varying frame design and connects previously known endpoint asymptotics.
